properties.publicTransport: Travel on public transport is free on Anzac Day for veterans and families. Additional early morning services will run. Buses will be diverting while roads are closed. Light rail services will not run between Town Hall and Circular Quay until 6.15am due to the Dawn Service, and may be temporarily held at stops or partially closed between 12.30pm and 1.30pm due to the March. Visit transportnsw.info for details.
properties.otherAdvice:
Major roads will be closed in the Sydney CBD for the Anzac Day Dawn Service in Martin Place from 4.20am and for the March on Elizabeth St from 9am. 

Motorists should avoid travelling through the CBD while roads are closed or expect delays and allow extra travel time. While roads are closed travel east/west across the CBD is maintained via Bridge St or via Goulburn St.

Key road closures:

  • From 2am to 4pm: Pitt St, George St and Castlereagh St between Hunter St and King St. A westbound section of Hunter St between Elizabeth St and Hamilton St. Hosking Pl from Castlereagh St.
  • From 2am to 6pm: Angel Pl and Ash St.
  • From 6am to 4pm: Major roads between Bridge St in Circular Quay and Goulburn St in the CBD South, including sections of Castlereagh St, Elizabeth St, King St, Market St, Pitt St, Margaret St, Hunter St, O’Connell St, Gresham St, Bent St, Park St, Bathurst St, Bligh St, Phillip St, Loftus St and Liverpool St.

There will be no managed vehicle access or access to/from driveways within the road closure footprint for the safety of participants and spectators. Pedestrians can cross the March route at the designated crossing point on Elizabeth St at Park St and Hunter St, and at underground crossings at Bathurst St, Museum Station and Martin Place Station.

Cycleway closures will be in place on Pitt St from 2am to 4pm, and on sections of Castlereagh St, King St, Liverpool St, Park St, Pitt St and Phillip St from 6am to 4pm.

Extensive special event clearway parking restrictions will be in effect on various major roads in the Sydney CBD from 1am around Martin Place and from 5.30am on other major roads. All major road closures and clearways are due to be lifted by 4pm.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents, businesses or TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies so check signs carefully on the day and the night before as clearways come into effect in the early morning. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

properties.publicTransport: Travel on public transport is included in tickets to the Show. Express trains and Major Event Buses will run daily. Regular route buses 525, 526, 533 and N81 in Olympic Park will use different stops while roads are closed. Visit transportnsw.info to plan your trip.
properties.otherAdvice:
Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to visit the annual Sydney Royal Easter Show over 12 days at Sydney Olympic Park from Friday 11 to Tuesday 22 April. 

  • Motorists should allow extra travel time on roads approaching the precinct including the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd throughout the show. 
  • It’s essential to pre-book parking online in advance. Car parks in Olympic Park are likely to sell out each day of the Show, so get in early and secure your parking space now. If you have pre-booked follow directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry.
  • Travel on transport is included in event tickets. Consider parking at a nearby station commuter carpark and continuing your trip by train or bus to Olympic Park. 

Road closures and changes to parklands are in place within the Sydney Olympic Park Precinct from Friday 28 March until Tuesday 29 April before, during and after the Easter Show including sections of Dawn Fraser Ave, Olympic Blvd, Showground Rd, Murray Rose Ave, Kevin Coombs Ave, Marjorie Jackson Pwy, Shirley Strickland Ave, Rod Laver Dr. Check out the Sydney Olympic Park Authority interactive map for more details.

Super Rugby: Waratahs v Chiefs at Allianz Stadium. Kick-off at 7:35pm, full-time approx 9:10pm.

Traffic may be heavier than usual on roads approaching Moore Park as fans travel to the match. Allow extra travel time on roads including the Eastern Distributor, Moore Park Rd, Cleveland St, Anzac Pde and Lang Rd.

Changed traffic conditions will be in place:

  • Driver Ave may be partially closed outside the stadium from 5.30pm and will reopen once crowds have safely cleared the area after the game.
  • No through-traffic will be available on Driver Avenue, however access to EP3 grass car park and drop-off areas maintained from Lang Rd. Car park open from 4.30pm. EP2 car park will not be open for this match.
  • Special event clearways will be in place on roads in Moore Park from 3pm to 11pm on sections of Albion St and Lang Rd, and from 6am to 11pm on Cleveland St and Fitzroy St.  

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types, and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.
